title: Seljuk Dynasty
capsule: The Seljuk dynasty originated among the Oghuz Turkic Qïnïq tribe, whose eponymous founder Seljuk ibn Duqaq migrated from the Eurasian steppe to the Jand region near the Syr Darya in the late tenth century and converted to Sunni Islam around 985 CE. His grandsons Tughril and Chaghri Beg began conquering Khorasan from the Ghaznavids after their decisive victory at the Battle of Dandanaqan in 1040, shortly after the period covered by this entry's 990–1040 attestation window. During the 990–1040 phase the Seljuks operated as a frontier ghazi confederation raiding into Transoxiana and Khorasan before emerging as a major power; the subsequent Great Seljuk Empire would eventually stretch from Central Asia to Anatolia and dominate the Abbasid caliphate. The dynasty's Persianate administrative culture shaped Islamic civilisation across the Middle East for two centuries.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The early Seljuk period (990–1040) before Dandanaqan is poorly documented in terms of territorial extent; their range was nomadic and fluid, so any mapped polygon for this phase is a very rough approximation.
